Welcome to Cambridge University Urdu Society! This is a platform for anyone with an appreciation of Urdu language, adab (literature) or shayari (poetry) to benefit from the rich literature which has been made foreign for us.

So whether you're a well versed poet, just discovering the wise words of Iqbal, or simply miss hearing Urdu while at Cambridge, this is the society for you! All levels of Urdu speakers are welcome and we aspire to make our events as inclusive as possible :)

We look forward to hosting speaker events, reading circles, socials and so much more! 

Follow us and watch this space for more updates coming soon!
.
.
.

Cambridge Qalamkaar (The Cambridge Writer) is a weekly newsletter for the promotion of Urdu language and its wealth of related literature, poetry and music. Every week we intend to provide you with interesting poetry and famous works of urdu literary personalities. Link to sign up is in the page bio. 

کیمبرج قلمکار اردو زبان اور اس سے وابستہ ادب، شاعری، اور موسیقی کے فروغ کے لئے ہے۔ ہماری کوشش رہے گی کہ آپ کو ہر ہفتہ دلچسپ نضمیں، شاعری، اور ادب سے منسلک مشہورشخصیات سے آگاہ رکھیں۔ 

Cambridge Qalamkār urdū zubān aur us se wābasta adab, shāyarī aur musīqī ke farogh ke liye hai. Hamārī koshish rahegī ke āp ko har hafta dilchasp nazmen, shāyari aur adab se munsalik mashhūr shakhsiyāt se āgāh rakhen.

Abeer, who is studying English at Lucy Cavendish, will be one of our Poetry Officers this year. 
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘As a literature student who has never traced Urdu words or seen an Urdu author in the curriculum, I want to connect with my roots again, and learn to have the same love for the language that my ancestors had.’

Fazal, who is studying Medicine at Downing, will be one of our Poetry Officers this year.
.
.
.
Why he joined the Committee: 
‘Urdu poetry is half my personality.’

Taha, who is studying for an MPhil in Modern South Asian Studies, will be our Language Officer this year. 
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘The language of love, urdu zabaan is an open call for a 'bazm' of lovers, those who have failed in love or are in love, finding love. The way, and all the meanings held within it, that it embraces the person in frenzy makes it all the more attractive for one to not love this language. Hence, the lost self is also trying to find meaning in the midst of chaos and desolation.’

Sobaan, who is studying Education at Selwyn, will be one of our Content and Media Officers this year. 
.
.
.
Why he joined the Committee: 
‘To share my love for Urdu poetry and music and of course the language itself! There really was a golden age of Urdu literature that sadly most young people don't know about, so I hope to shed some light on this and some of the famous poets and singers of the past.’

Savannah, who is studying Philosophy of Science at Magdalene, will be one of our Content and Media Officers this year. 
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘I love how poetic Urdu is as a language, as well as the history of it and how it diverged from the proto-Indo-European language. I went to school in Birmingham where many of my friends speak Urdu and it’s so nice when I surprise their parents with a lil bit of Urdu skills!’

Aatqa, who is studying Medicine at Newnham, is our Graphics and Publicity Officer. 
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘To improve my language abilities, in particular my reading and writing:) I'm looking forward to meet and hang out with people who are interested in the beauty of the Urdu and the cultures and histories associated with it!’

Samiha, who is studying Law at Gonville and Caius, will be our Treasurer this year. 
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
'We founded this society to create a platform for students to facilitate their growing interest in Urdu language, literature, culture and its history. Urdu being such a beautiful language, it automatically lends itself to having very deep-rooted poetry.'

Mahwish, who is a PhD candidate for Computer Science at Hughes Hall, will be our General Secretary.
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘For the love of language and connect with those who share this love’

Hanniya, who is studying Architecture at Murray Edwards, is our Vice President.
.
.
.
Why she joined the Committee: 
‘This society stemmed from a desire to understand and connect with my culture and language, which I feel I wasn’t able to fully appreciate growing up. I hope this can become a space where we can learn from one another and collectively deepen our knowledge and understanding of what Urdu has to offer.’

Hassan, who is a PhD candidate for Earth Sciences at Selwyn, is our President. 
.
.
.
Why he joined the Committee: 
‘To appreciate the beauty of Urdu and emphasise how using it aesthetically makes it a work of art’

Piyam-e-Iqbal: Join us in conversation with Zirrar Ali on the poetry, legacy and philosophy of Allama Iqbal, followed by a Q&A.

پیامِ اقبال: ‎آئیے اقبال کی شاعری، فلسفے، اور ‎میراث سے متعلق گفتگو کے لئے شامل ہوں ضرار علی کے ساتھ! آپ کے پاس سوالات پوچھنے اور ضرار کی کتاب غازی و گلستان خریدنے کا موقع بھی ہوگا!

The event will take place in the Sidgwick Hall at Newnham College. 
.
.
.
The discussion will be followed by an opportunity to purchase Zirrar’s latest book ‘Ghazi and the Garden’, a modern translation of Iqbal’s poetry. ‘Considered by many to be the last of the great classical Persian poets, and among the first modern Muslim philosophers, Iqbal’s work has been pivotal in anti-colonial movements and revolutions throughout the Muslim world in the 20th century. Though he is a household name in the Indian subcontinent, Iran and Turkey, this translation is highly valuable to English readers. This collection brings together some of his most poignant and powerful Urdu poems taken from Bang-e Dra (Call of the Marching Bell) and Bal-e Jibreel (Gabriel’s Wing), as well as some of his finest Persian ghazals from Zabur-e Ajam (Persian Psalms).’

اردو شاعری تشبیہ، کنایہ اور استعارہ کے وسیع  و عمدہ  استعمال کے حوالے سے جانی جاتی ہے۔  ہم آپ کو اس نظم کے ذریعے ایسی ایک مثال سے متعارف کرواتے ہیں۔گُُل اور بلبل، جس میں  عاشق کی تشبیہ بلبل ، اور معشوق کی تشبیہ گل سے دی گئی ہے ۔ 

اس شعر میں شاعر محبوب کے لیے اپنی محبت کا موازنہ  بلبل کی گل سے محبت سے کرتا ہے ۔

Urdu poetry is known for its rich use of similes, metaphors, and symbolism. Through this poem we’ll introduce you to one such example: the gul (rose) and bulbul (nightingale) where the latter  represents the lover, and the rose represents the beloved. 

In the couplet, the poet compares the love that he has for his beloved to the sincere love of the nightingale for the rose. See our newsletter for a link to a paper to explore the imagery some more!

Aqib Sabir is a poet, researcher, and translator. He is one of the young poets from India who rose to recognition with the digital turn in Urdu poetry. What does it mean to awaken the self through beauty? Delivered by his grandson Walid Iqbal, this lecture explores Mohammed’s Iqbal’s poetics of awakening, his vision of the self cultivated through love, striving and creative action, and how his poetry built bridges across traditions and civilisations. @cambridgeurdusoc 
Tickets go live on Eventbrite from 1 October.

posts.caption:
What is the true meaning of love and beauty?
Independent scholar Hina Khalid explores how poet-philosopher Muhammad Iqbal saw love as the living fabric of creation. In his work, beauty is not just something to look at, it is a vibrant spark that calls us closer to the divine.
Discover more in Hina’s new book, Words of Witness: Divine Call and Human Response in Iqbal and Tagore, published by Brill .
Tickets go live on Eventbrite from 1 October.

#cfia #thecambridgefestivalofislamicarts
